concepts.def: East Yorkshire coast, around 60 km from Flamborough to Spurn.
Averages around 2 m per year, the fastest in Europe.
Weak glacial till slumps easily when wet, speeding cliff retreat.
Sea walls, groynes and rip-rap defend places like Mappleton.
Beach nourishment and dune planting work with nature.
Letting some land flood, e.g. at Medmerry in West Sussex. 🌊

walkthroughs.body_html:
The Holderness coast runs ~60 km along East Yorkshire.

It loses roughly 2 m a year, making it Europe's fastest-eroding coast.

Soft boulder clay cliffs slump after rain.

Defences vary along the coast.

Mappleton got rock groynes and a revetment in 1991.

But trapping sediment starved Cowden to the south — defences shifted the problem.

Modern policy often favours working with nature.

Beach nourishment adds sand; managed retreat lets low-value land flood.

Example: Medmerry realignment in West Sussex (2013) created saltmarsh and flood storage.
